doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: First gigs at 16 and Jimmy Walsh's band at Casino Gardens
summary: He joined the union, worked weekends and singer jobs, then played with Jimmy Walsh and arranged for Jan Savitt.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So was it before you left or after that you first started playing out in ensembles?

Well I moved to Los Angeles, I was 16, so I joined the union there. And I was still going to school, I would work weekends, club dates they would call them. It wasn’t — I mean not a lot of guys want to take a chance on a 16-year-old, but my dad knew, people knew him and so he contacted people, and I got to working. Piano players you know can do so many things. I played in a couple of places where it was piano alone with vocalists, and as soon as I graduated high school, which I was 17 when I graduated, then I got to working steady like doing that. It was kind of like cocktail place that had singers, and you’d play for them. And oh I don’t know if anybody remembers Jimmy Walsh, that was the first band that I got to play with. And that was at the Casino Gardens, that’s kind of famous, in Ocean Park. So that was my first band. He had a good band, he played trombone very good. Like about a 12-piece. You know it’s a ballroom, Casino Gardens. Well see one thing — I didn’t play with any name people. I arranged for Jan Savitt, before I went in the service. I was 19 when I went in the service. So I arranged for Jan Savitt and just when I got my draft notice, he sent me a telegram to come and join the band right at that time.
